theme: The CN Tower, one tiny step at a time
callback: The tower gets its own licence plate

events.text: I booked us tickets for the CN Tower. Glass floor, lookout, the whole Toronto postcard.
Excellent. I’ll bring our emotional support snack.
A granola bar?
No. I’ve made the tower a licence plate: THE 6IX. It’s how we know it’s ours.
It’s already the tallest thing in the room, and now it has vanity plates.
I read the CN Tower was the world’s tallest freestanding structure for more than three decades.
That is a very long time to be the tallest person at a party.
Then someone taller arrived, and the tower had to be gracious about it.
I can relate. I was tallest in my family until my cousin got new shoes.
Let’s get double-doubles. We’re going to need steady hands for the glass floor.
We need snacks for the tower. Something portable, not crumbly, not loud.
So… a grape with good manners?
The glass floor is a psychological negotiation! Bring a banana. It’s naturally curved, so it knows how to handle a drop.
That’s not how bananas work, but I respect the confidence.
Buy two. One for courage, one for the banana’s counsel.
We’re getting apples. They’ve been quietly dependable this whole time.
The glass floor was incredible. I could see the streets way down there—and my own shoes having a separate opinion.
You stepped out first. Then you held my hand like you were guiding me across a very high, very transparent puddle.
And you stepped out too. That’s the whole trick: we can be nervous at the same time.
The EdgeWalk is outside the tower, clipped into a safety system. I admire it from the inside, with both feet and a window between us.
The revolving restaurant turns slowly enough to enjoy the view. We could eat there someday.
Perfect. We’ll get a table by the window, share dessert, and let the city do the walking.
And the tower’s licence plate?
THE 6IX. It can drive us home. We’ll take the streetcar.
